battle.name: 第一次鱈魚戰爭
battle.theater: 冰島沿岸及鄰近北大西洋
battle.brief: 第一次鱈魚戰爭於1958年3月爆發，冰島因漁業管轄範圍與英國發生衝突，交鋒集中在冰島沿岸及附近北大西洋，英方與冰島海岸警衛隊多次對抗。Gatling gun（加特林機槍）並非本戰爭所用武器，但美國陸軍於1860年將其列裝，時間明顯早於本戰爭爆發之年。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: 加特林機槍是美國陸軍早期制式的旋轉式多管機槍，配置於步兵支援與固定陣位，負責持續壓制及據點防禦；重型機槍普及後，主要轉作後方警戒。

countries: 1958年6月1日，北大西洋冰島沿岸的漁業管轄爭議演變成第一次鱈魚戰爭，直接對抗的兩方是冰島與英國。英方以皇家海軍 Daring 級驅逐艦 Dainty、Dacota 及其護航的拖網船隊參與，冰方則由海岸警衛隊的 Þór、Óðinn 執行巡邏、攔截、登船與扣留。交會集中在冰島沿岸十二海里線及其外側的國際水域，沒有登陸戰，也沒有固定陸戰線。英方把漁船隊能否在特定水域航行與捕魚視為海權爭端的實際問題，冰方則把新界線內的巡航、停船、扣船和排船視作國家管轄權的執行，因此這是一場由國家船舶直接進行的近距離海上對峙，而不是大型艦隊之間的決戰。
countriesEn: On 1 June 1958, a fisheries-jurisdiction dispute around Iceland in the North Atlantic developed into the First Cod War, with Iceland and the United Kingdom as the two opposing sides. Britain participated through the Royal Navy Daring-class destroyers Dainty and Dacota and the trawler fleet they escorted, while Iceland relied on the Coast Guard vessels Þór and Óðinn for patrol, interception, boarding and seizure. The encounters were concentrated along Iceland's twelve-mile line and in the international waters immediately outside it; there was no landing and no fixed land front. Britain treated the trawlers' ability to navigate and fish in the designated grounds as the practical issue in a dispute over maritime rights, while Iceland regarded patrolling, stopping vessels, seizure and exclusion within its new line as the exercise of national jurisdiction. The result was therefore a close-range maritime confrontation conducted by state ships rather than a decisive battle between large fleets.
people: 擴界命令發出時，冰島總理是 Davíð Oddsson；他於7月4日由 Ólafur Jóhannesson 接任，後者延續並鞏固十二海里政策。英國方面，首相 Harold Macmillan 與外交大臣 Selwyn Lloyd 負責處理冰島通告、提出外交異議及評估護航，海軍派遣則由英國海軍部在 First Sea Lord John Eccles 任內啟動，年中轉由 Alexander Grant 接手。冰島方面，海岸警衛隊隊長及 Þór、Óðinn 的值班船長決定迫停、登船與拖返雷克雅未克；英方則由 Dainty、Dacota 艦長決定警告射擊、追蹤、隊形與護航距離。政治部門控制談判底線，海軍司令部決定是否派遣兵力海上指揮則控制交戰節奏，這種分層指揮使雙方能對漁船施壓，同時避免立即把漁業摩擦擴大為正式戰爭。
peopleEn: When the extension order was issued, Davíð Oddsson was prime minister of Iceland; he was succeeded on 4 July by Ólafur Jóhannesson, who continued and consolidated the twelve-mile policy. In Britain, Prime Minister Harold Macmillan and Foreign Secretary Selwyn Lloyd handled Iceland's notification, diplomatic objections and the assessment of naval protection, while the Admiralty initiated the dispatch of warships during the tenure of First Sea Lord John Eccles, with Alexander Grant taking over later in 1958. On the Icelandic side, the Coast Guard commander and the watch captains of Þór and Óðinn decided when to stop, board and tow vessels back to Reykjavík. The captains of Dainty and Dacota controlled warning fire, tracking, formation and escort distance. Political departments set the negotiating limits, the naval command decided whether to deploy ships, and commanders at sea regulated the encounters, allowing pressure on the trawlers without immediately turning a fisheries dispute into a declared war.
kits: 冰方的兩艘主力是1955年前後投入海岸警衛隊的 Þór 與 Óðinn；Þór 約530噸、船長約55.5公尺、巡航速度約14節，Óðinn 約380噸、屬五十公尺級巡艇，巡航約13節。兩艇的主要武裝包括40公厘 Bofors 自動炮與20公厘 Oerlikon 機炮，另有北約標準無線電、救生與近海巡邏設備。英方 Dainty、Dacota 均屬 Daring 級，裝有4.5英寸 QF 主炮、40公厘 Bofors 防空炮、21英寸魚雷發射管、深水炸彈投射器及 Type 965 對空搜索雷達；拖網船則多為蒸汽側拖網船，船上以蒸汽絞車、拖網鋼纜、鍋爐燃料、淡水與無線電維持長距離作業。40公厘與20公厘炮彈、4.5英寸炮彈、魚雷和深水炸彈均已列裝，但除英方警告射擊外，沒有可靠紀錄顯示冰方曾向英艦或人員射出炮彈。警告射擊使用的是實彈或空包彈，主要史料記載不一，因此不能把它寫成已命中的戰鬥射擊。
kitsEn: Iceland's two principal vessels were Þór and Óðinn, which entered Coast Guard service around 1955. Þór was approximately 530 tons, 55.5 metres long and capable of about 14 knots, while Óðinn was approximately 380 tons, was a fifty-metre-class patrol vessel and cruised at about 13 knots. Their principal armament included Bofors 40 mm automatic cannon and Oerlikon 20 mm cannon, supplemented by NATO-standard radio, lifesaving and coastal-patrol equipment. Dainty and Dacota were both Daring-class destroyers fitted with 4.5-inch QF main guns, Bofors 40 mm anti-aircraft guns, 21-inch torpedo tubes, depth-charge projectors and Type 965 air-search radar. The trawlers were predominantly steam side trawlers, supported by steam winches, trawl wire, boiler fuel, fresh water and radio for long-distance operations. Ammunition for the 40 mm and 20 mm guns, the 4.5-inch guns, torpedoes and depth charges was all in service, but no reliable record shows that the Icelandic guns fired on British ships or personnel. The British warning discharge was not consistently described as live or blank ammunition, so it cannot be presented as a confirmed combat hit.
tactics: 6月4日，Þór 在冰島海岸外約10海里、即18.5公里處攔住英國拖網船 Apollo。該位置在冰島新主張的十二海里線內，Þór 先以無線電要求停船，再逼近船身，以接觸碰撞降低 Apollo 的航速，登船組隨即登船控制，並把漁船拖回雷克雅未克。6月6日，Óðinn 又攔截並登船 British trawler John。6月中旬，Dainty 與 Dacota 進入爭議海域，以搜索雷達與目視追蹤漁船隊，護航編隊在冰島巡邏艇附近保持可反應距離；英方也曾從4.5英寸主炮打出越過 Þór 艇首的警告射擊，公開資料沒有確認炮彈命中船體或人員。7月至8月的接觸主要是追蹤、橫向迫使漁船改向、警告、登船與拖返，而非追求擊沉。冰方受船程、燃油與岸上補給限制，常以兩艇輪流接替；英方則靠較長航程與海軍補給維持存在。雙方沒有形成大規模炮戰，海上對抗與外交接觸自夏季起並行。
tacticsEn: On 4 June, Þór intercepted the British trawler Apollo about 10 nautical miles, or 18.5 kilometres, off Iceland. The position lay within Iceland's newly claimed twelve-mile line. Þór first ordered the vessel to stop by radio, then closed the distance and used hull contact to reduce Apollo's speed while the boarding party went aboard, took control and towed the trawler back to Reykjavík. On 6 June, Óðinn intercepted and boarded another British trawler, John. In mid-June, Dainty and Dacota entered the disputed area, tracking the trawler formation with search radar and visual observation while preserving enough distance to react if the Icelandic patrol vessels approached. British ships also fired a 4.5-inch warning discharge across the bow of Þór, although the surviving record does not confirm that the projectile struck a hull or person. Contacts during July and August centred on shadowing, forcing trawlers to alter course by crossing their bows, issuing warnings, boarding and towing rather than attempting to sink vessels. Iceland's limited range, fuel endurance and shore replenishment requirements led the two patrol ships to relieve one another, while Britain maintained presence through longer endurance and naval supply. There was no large-scale gun battle, and maritime pressure developed alongside diplomatic contact from the summer onward.
data: 這場對抗可分成三個時間點：6月1日是冰島宣布把漁業界線由四海里擴至十二海里的法律起點，6月4日 Þór 攔截 Apollo 是第一宗實際接觸，11月11日則通常被視為戰爭的實際終點，三個日期相隔160天。十二海里等於22.2公里，舊的四海里界線則是7.4公里；首宗事發位置約10海里，正好落在兩條線之間。冰方主要有 Þór、Óðinn 兩艇，英方主要有 Dainty、Dacota 兩艘驅逐艦，另 有拖網船隊參與。可確定至少 Apollo 與 John 被扣留，六月底及夏季另有攔查與扣船，但不同資料對被扣漁船總數的記載不一致，因此不列一個未經核實的總數。主要史料沒有確認任何人死亡，受傷人數亦無一致資料；能確認的是沒有英國或冰島軍艦被擊沉，警告炮沒有已證實的人員命中，碰撞與控制行動造成的破損亦屬有限。
dataEn: The confrontation can be divided into three reference points: 1 June was the legal beginning when Iceland announced the extension of its fisheries line from four to twelve nautical miles, 4 June, when Þór intercepted Apollo, was the first physical contact, and 11 November is generally treated as the effective end, a span of 160 days. Twelve nautical miles equals 22.2 kilometres, while the former four-mile limit was 7.4 kilometres; the first incident occurred about 10 nautical miles offshore, directly between those lines. Iceland's principal force consisted of Þór and Óðinn, while Britain's principal warships were the destroyers Dainty and Dacota, accompanied by a trawler fleet. At least Apollo and John were seized, with further interceptions and seizures recorded in late June and during the summer, although sources disagree on the total number of vessels detained. Major accounts do not confirm any deaths, and there is no consistent figure for injuries. What can be confirmed is that neither a British nor an Icelandic warship was sunk, the warning gun discharge has no confirmed personnel hit, and collision or control operations produced limited damage.
cause: 衝突源於英冰對漁業權的既有理解與冰島新管轄主張不一致。冰島在1948年把漁業界線設為四海里，1949年英冰協議則處理英國拖網船在此界線外作業的權利、配額與管理方式；到1958年，冰島未先與英國完成談判，便把界線一次擴至十二海里。同年《日內瓦公海公約》把十二海里領海界線納入新近形成的海洋法框架，但公約的簽署、生效與英冰既有漁業協議是不同層次，不能自動解決原有配額和歷史作業問題。英方認為單方面改線破壞既得安排，冰島則把新線視為維護資源管轄的必要措施。實際失誤控制則在於雙方船隻都近岸活動，拖船、登船、警告與護航同時發生，而每次事件都留下是否追問、扣船或派遣驅逐艦的問題，使有限爭議逐步累積成持續五個月的對峙。
causeEn: The conflict arose from a mismatch between existing Anglo-Icelandic understandings of fishing rights and Iceland's new jurisdictional claim. Iceland established a four-mile fisheries line in 1948, and the 1949 Anglo-Icelandic agreement addressed British trawler operations outside that line, including access, quotas and administration. In 1958 Iceland extended the line to twelve nautical miles without first completing negotiations with Britain. The Geneva Convention on the High Sea of 1958 placed a twelve-mile territorial-sea limit within a developing maritime-law framework, but signature, entry into force and the existing Anglo-Icelandic fisheries agreement were separate matters and did not automatically settle inherited quotas or traditional operations. Britain regarded the unilateral change as an infringement of established arrangements, while Iceland treated the new line as necessary for resource jurisdiction. Practical loss of control developed because both sides operated close to shore and towing, boarding, warning fire and escorting occurred simultaneously. Each incident then raised the question of protest, seizure or further naval dispatch, gradually turning a limited dispute into a confrontation lasting five months.
impact: 夏季的實際結果顯示，兩艘冰島巡邏艇雖不足以控制整片北大西洋，卻能依靠岸基通信、接力巡邏與登船拖返，在相當程度上迫使英方漁船停止不受干擾的作業。Dainty、Dacota 能保護部分漁船，卻也因貼近冰島小艇而增加碰撞風險，沒有取得可長期維持的制海效果。這次對峙促使英冰回到正式談判，顯示單靠護航或扣船都不能確定漁業權的法律基礎。1961年的《英冰臨時協議》才正式處理核心爭議：英國承認冰島的十二海里界線，冰島則在冰方監管下給英國漁船有條件的作業權，並把英國年度捕魚量限制在約十三萬噸。協議沒有消除所有配額與權利爭議，但把1958年的海上對抗轉為可協商的期限、數量與管理問題，也證明海岸警衛隊的日常存在與海軍護航同樣會影響國家談判。
impactEn: The practical results of the summer showed that two Icelandic patrol vessels could not control the whole North Atlantic, but they could use shore-based communications, relief rotations, boarding and towing to disrupt unescorted British fishing to a significant degree. Dainty and Dacota could protect some trawlers, yet their proximity to the smaller Icelandic ships increased collision risks and did not produce lasting control. The confrontation pushed both governments back into formal negotiations and demonstrated that neither escort duty nor seizure alone could settle the legal basis of fishing access. The core dispute was addressed in 1961 by the Anglo-Icelandic Interim Agreement: Britain recognised Iceland's twelve-mile limit, while Iceland permitted British fishing under Icelandic administration and limited the British annual catch to approximately 130,000 tonnes. The agreement did not erase every question of quotas and rights, but it converted the confrontation of 1958 into negotiable questions of duration, quantity and administration. It also demonstrated that the daily presence of a coast guard, like the deployment of naval escorts, could shape state-level negotiations.
result: 11月11日被定為第一次鱈魚戰爭的實際終點。英方不再在爭議海域維持對拖網船的持續直接護航，涉事漁船離開或停止原來的作業方式，被扣留的船隻也在危機解除後獲釋，沒有被永久扣作戰利品。1958年的結束並非由正式停戰條約或永久性的權利讓步構成：英國當時尚未以協議全面承認冰島的新界線，具體的漁業條件則留待談判，最終由1961年的臨時協議處理。直接結果是冰島得以在十二海里內持續執行攔查與扣船，而英國以暫時停止受護航的爭議作業換取談判時間；英國漁船後來仍可在配額和指定條件下作業。整場衝突沒有形成陸地佔領、沒有軍艦沉沒，也沒有得到可靠資料確認的死亡人數，因此較準確的結論是冰島取得近海執法成果、英國避免持續升級，兩國再以協議取代海上對抗。
resultEn: 11 November is generally regarded as the effective end of the First Cod War. Britain ceased maintaining direct naval escorts for trawlers in the disputed area, the vessels involved left or stopped operating in the manner that had produced the confrontation, and the seized ships were released after the crisis rather than permanently retained as prizes. The war of 1958 did not end through a formal armistice or a permanent transfer of rights: Britain had not yet fully accepted Iceland's new limit through an agreement, and the practical fishing terms were left to negotiation, ultimately addressed in the 1961 Interim Agreement. The immediate result was that Iceland could continue enforcing interception and seizure within twelve miles, while Britain obtained time by suspending the contested escorted operations that had provoked the incidents. British fishing later continued subject to quotas and designated conditions. There was no territorial occupation, no sinking of a warship and no death figure confirmed by reliable evidence. The most accurate assessment is therefore operational Icelandic enforcement combined with British avoidance of further escalation, followed by agreement in place of continuing maritime confrontation.
